titles.to: The Last Night on the Water

replace.find: She looked at her sneakers. “A little. The smell. The gulls.”
replace.with: She looked at her sneakers. “Ata, I was born after it left. I remember your stories. The gulls in them.”

replace.find: with a mineral tang she knew from childhood visits to Chimgan reservoirs and from nothing else. Salt.
replace.with: with a mineral tang she had never smelled in her life and knew anyway. Salt.

replace.find: Salinity twelve grams per liter. Twelve. Not Caspian, not Aral old. Something else. Something—”
replace.with: Salinity twelve grams per liter. Twelve. Nearly the old Aral, the Aral of 1960, before the rivers were taken for cotton. What is left out west is brine, a hundred grams and more. This is not that. This is—”

replace.find: The house smelled of damp wool when Aysulu woke.
replace.with: The house smelled of damp wool when Aysulu woke. She had come up from the shore after the boat and slept two hours like a stone.

replace.find:
"Good. The sea kept you awake last night, eh? It talks."

"I didn't hear it," she said.
replace.with:
"Good. The sea kept you awake all night, eh? It talks."

"I only heard it breathe," she said.

replace.find:
The new shore was already loud when they came down the track.

Aysulu had expected a few boats. What she found was a whole street laid along the water.
replace.with:
The new shore was louder than at dawn when they came down the track.

At dawn Aysulu had walked the line half asleep. Now, in full morning, it had grown into a whole street laid along the water.

replace.find: A boy Aysulu recognized from yesterday ran up
replace.with: A boy Aysulu recognized from the cliff last night ran up

replace.find: "You row well for a sack of flour," Oralbay said.
replace.with: "You sit well in a boat for a sack of flour," Oralbay said.

replace.find:
"When you were small you were afraid of the cannery horn. You would cover your ears and run to me. Do you remember?"

"I remember the smell. Fish and smoke. And the girls singing on the steps."
replace.with:
"When you were small you were afraid of the camels. When they bellowed you would cover your ears and run to me. Do you remember?"

"I remember your stories. The cannery. Fish and smoke. The girls singing on the steps."

replace.find: "Yesterday I took you where they used to sing. Did you feel it?"
replace.with: "This morning I took you where they used to sing. Did you feel it?"

replace.find: Your father was born in that room. Your grandmother died in that bed while the sea was leaving. She said to me, Oralbay, do not follow yet. Live and bury me high where water cannot take me. So I lived.
replace.with: Your mother was born in that room. Your grandmother went out on the water the autumn the sea began to leave, and it did not give her back. Long before, she said to me, Oralbay, if the sea takes me first, do not follow yet. Live. So I lived.

replace.find: the tremor she had not noticed yesterday when he rowed
replace.with: the tremor she had not noticed that morning when he rowed

replace.find: She thought of rowing yesterday, the cold bite at her calves
replace.with: She thought of the boat that morning, the cold bite at her calves

replace.find:
"It came Thursday," Oralbay said. He did not look at her. "You slept through the best part."

"I did not sleep," she said.

She remembered it anyway the way he had told it that morning, and the telling had become hers. How there had been no wave and no noise,
replace.with:
"It came Thursday," Oralbay said. He did not look at her. "Last night it was new. Tonight it is ours."

She remembered every minute of it. No wave and no noise,

replace.find: She had woken to gulls and to Rybak shouting her grandfather's name in the street.
replace.with: She had felt it in her chest then. She felt it again now.

replace.find: "At dawn yesterday," Oralbay said, "you should have seen." He pointed with his chin. "They laid out carp on tarps. Big ones. Zhaksy. The buyers pressed close. I bought two for soup."
replace.with: "This morning's carp," Oralbay said, and pointed with his chin. "Big as my arm. Zhaksy. Tomorrow they will be bigger. The sea gives its best at the end."

replace.find: Aysulu remembered that dawn too. She had gone down with her plastic bag because he had asked, because her sneakers were still damp and she wanted to be useful. The air had been milky and cold. The boats were low wooden batils she did not recognize, painted blue and white, with names in faded Cyrillic. The men in them wore canvas jackets and spoke Karakalpak with words she had to turn over twice to understand, jokes about quotas and a foreman named Daulet. Their faces were gray with work. One had a scar split through his eyebrow. When she paid, his palm was rough and his change was coins dated 1968.
replace.with: Aysulu thought of the market in full light that morning: the low green boats, the quilted jackets from the school photograph, the fishermen's jokes about quotas and a foreman named Daulet, and coins changing hands that were dated 1968.

replace.find: She had not known then. She had carried the fish home swinging in the bag and thought about ice. It was Rybak who told her later by the cannery wall, his glasses fogged, his clipboard shaking, that Daulet had died in a storm in November 1968 and that the crew list matched the names on the town monument.
replace.with: It was Rybak who told her the rest that afternoon by the cannery wall, his glasses fogged, his clipboard shaking: Daulet had died in a storm in November 1968, and the crew list matched the names in the cannery's old memorial book.

replace.find: "We worked the Muynak cannery fleet.
replace.with: "We worked the Moynaq cannery fleet.

replace.find: "Four centimeters since morning," he said in Russian. His voice was hoarse. "Same as yesterday. No inflow
replace.with: "Eleven centimeters since morning," he said in Russian. His voice was hoarse. "Steady as a clock. No inflow

replace.find: "I cancelled the buyer," she said.
replace.with: "I am not calling the buyer back," she said.

replace.find: painting the gunwale of his batil which sat on trestles by the shed,
replace.with: painting the gunwale of his skiff, which he had hauled up onto trestles by the shed,

replace.find: He told her about the cannery girls who used to sing on the steps to keep time with the knives, how their voices carried across the roadstead on still evenings.
replace.with: He told her the Karakalpak names of the winds, one for each direction.

replace.find: "Here," he said. "The cannery dock. The girls sat there." He pointed to nothing she could see. "My wife worked the second table. She sang lower than the others. I could pick her out."
replace.with: "Here again," he said. "Yesterday I did not tell you what is under us. The cannery dock. The girls sat on its steps." He pointed to nothing she could see. "My wife sang the second voice, the loudest on the steps. I could pick her out from any boat."

replace.find: the crane skeletons, the memorial needle,
replace.with: the crane skeletons, the stone sailor on the memorial,

replace.find:
The words came clean. "I never told you. In Tashkent I said I would learn. I did not."

He nodded. "I know. You hold the boat like it will bite."
replace.with:
The words came clean. "You guessed it yesterday. But I never said it to you myself. For years I told myself I would learn. I did not."

He nodded. "I know. You still hold the boat like it will bite."

replace.find: "You left one in Tashkent when you were twelve. Your mother was angry. I kept it."
replace.with: "You dropped it in the yard the day you left for Tashkent. You were twelve. The other one went with you. I kept this one."

replace.find: The batil floated ten steps out
replace.with: The skiff floated ten steps out

replace.find: The tin cup burned her palms in the best way.
replace.with: A tin cup burned her palms in the best way.

replace.find: No slap beyond the wall. No gulls.
replace.with: No slap beyond the wall.

replace.find: the waterline on the batil where
replace.with: the waterline on the skiff where

notes: Fixed ch3 retelling the sea's return and the dawn market as unseen/new (she watched both in ch1), the swim confession and cannery-singing trip repeated as new, grandmother's death (bed vs drowned per brief), father/mother slip, 'yesterday' timeline drift in ch2, batil/skiff naming, lost tin cup reused, memorial needle vs stone sailor, near-duplicate titles; history: Aysulu (b. ~1997) cannot remember the sea, salinity line now accurate (old Aral ~10 g/L, western brine 100+).

replace.find: We will shape it round like a baby doll and sit it on a stump.
replace.with: We will shape it round like a little doll and sit it on a stump.

replace.find: “Water is for sharing. Work is for sharing too. Tomorrow we will see your paws in the mud.”
replace.with: “Water is for sharing. Work is for sharing too. Tomorrow we dig the well deeper, so it never runs dry. We will see your paws in the mud.”

replace.find: He held the little gum friend on his knee.
replace.with: He sat the little gum friend on the stump beside him.

replace.find: Now, you have heard this tale from the start, so let us tell it true all in one string.
replace.with:
"Tell the whole tale, Tante," said Bouki. "For the egg. Eggs like stories."

So Tante Tortue sat down on a cypress knee and told it true, all in one string. You can listen too.

replace.find: "Shovels are for turtles," he sang. "Shovels are for fools. I never get thirsty. That is my rule."
replace.with: "Shovels are heavy," he sang. "Shovels are slow. I will nap while you go, go, go!"

replace.find: Lapin played a tune on a reed. Toot, toot, toot. Bouki spun faster and faster till down he went.
replace.with: Lapin clapped a tune. Clap, clap, clap. Bouki spun faster and faster till down he sat.

replace.find: Three nights the same. Dance, snore, empty bucket.
replace.with: Next morning, the same. Empty bucket, round prints.

replace.find: "Bonjour, little friend," he said, for Lapin says hello to everybody. "You will not tell if I take a drink?"
replace.with: "Bonsoir, little friend," he said, for Lapin says hello to everybody. "Will you not say bonsoir back?"

replace.find: Lapin touched it. Stick. His paw would not come free. Pop.
replace.with: Lapin shook its hand. Stick. His paw would not come free.

replace.find: Bouki woke up. He did not laugh. He lifted Lapin gentle. Pop, pop went the paws. He held Lapin's tin cup while Lapin drank cool water. Glug.
replace.with: Bouki came running. He did not laugh. He held Lapin's tin cup while Lapin drank cool water. Glug. Then Tante Tortue warmed the gum soft, and pop, pop went the paws.

replace.find: wrapped the shiny egg in her lace shawl to keep it soft.
replace.with: wrapped the shiny egg in her lace shawl to keep it warm.

notes: Retitled three chapters all called 'The Empty Bucket'; framed the ch4 recap as Tante telling the tale to the egg and made it match chs 1-2 (song, clapping not reed, one dance night, bonsoir, Tante frees the paws); gave the ch3 digging a reason; removed 'baby doll' near the banned phrase ('tar baby' never appears).

replace.find: Posy woke up to a terrible noise.
replace.with: Posy woke up to a terrible noise. Again.

replace.find: The blue button glinted on the sill.
replace.with: The blue button glinted on the sill. She tucked it into her pocket.

replace.find: He looked at the crinkly whiskery shadow by the pole.
replace.with: He looked at the crinkly whiskery shadow peeking out again from behind his lamp pole.

replace.find: His singing voice was very bad and very kind.
replace.with: His voice was wobbly and very kind.

replace.find: silliest crossed eyed face
replace.with: silliest cross-eyed face
